question: Recall that, for any non-zero complex number $w$ which does not lie on the negative real axis, $\arg w$ denotes the unique real number $\theta$ in $(-\pi,\pi)$ such that $w=|w|(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)$. Let $z$ be any complex number such that its real and imaginary parts are both non-zero. Further, suppose that $z$ satisfies the relations $\arg z>\arg(z+1)$ and $\arg z>\arg(z+i)$. Then $\cos(\arg z)$ can take

options.A: any value in the set $(-1/2,0)\cup(0,1/2)$ but none from outside;
options.B: any value in the interval $(-1,0)$ but none from outside;
options.C: any value in the interval $(0,1)$ but none from outside;
options.D: any value in the set $(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$ but none from outside.
